To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the loop5 targeting inhibitors of Kinesins-5 differentially control the motor's motility and microtubules depolymerase activities.

small molecules can differentially control the microtubules interacting activities of Eg5, that these activities can be separated from motility, and that the depolymerase function is required for the formation of the mitotic microtubule array.
small molecule allosteric agents that inhibit the motility activity of human Kinesin5 are also capable of differentially controlling the depolymerase function of the motor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the allosteric regulation of Kinesin motor activity and the functional consequences of these effects.
the discovery of novel small molecule allosteric modulators of Kinesin motors and the development of a new paradigm to understand how these molecules impact the cellular function.
understanding the mechanism of action of small molecules that target Kinesin-6 motors, and the functional consequences of these effects on the mitotic spindle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the loop5 targeting inhibitors of Kinesins-5 do not all have the same effect on the motor and that the loop5-targeting agents are able to independently control the motile activity and microtubular dynamics of the motor.
the Eg5 microtuble depolymerizing and motile activities are differentially regulated by allosteric inhibitors and that the depolymerase is a distinct functional activity of the motor.
the small-molecule allosteric uncouples microtubule motility from microtubule microtubule interactions in Kinesin-6 during spindle assembly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the small molecule inhibitors of Eg5 can differentially modulate its multiple microtubule binding activities, and that these activities may not be functionally equivalent.
the Eg5 motor domain is capable of more that one type of interaction with microtubules and that these different activities can be differentially controlled by small molecules.
the Eg5 motor is capable of more types of interactions with the microtubules than previously recognized, and that these activities are differentially controlled by small molecule inhibitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Kinesin-2 and Kinesin-13 inhibitors can be used to probe the function of Eg5, and the use of Kinesin inhibitors to probe the function and regulation of Kinesin family members should be approached with caution.
small molecule allosteric inhibitors of Kinesins are likely to have a more complicated effect on the mitotic spindle than simply inhibiting motility.
Kinesin-6 motors are capable of more than just motility and that the microtubules themselves are more than a track for the motor.
